Hi Katie  thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our HIPAA eligibility discussion: 

Summary of what we heard
- Use case: clinical documentation ingestion and retrieval (clinic notes, patient IDs, limited lab results).
- Data types: PHI will include patient identifiers (name, DOB, MRN), clinical notes, and test results. No image PHI in scope right now.
- Key requirements: BAA required, encryption (in transit + at rest), customer-managed keys preferred, audit logging and exportable audit trail, and the ability to keep data within our US region.

Redwood eligibility & notes (high level)
- BAA availability: Redwood can execute a BAA for customers on Dedicated and Private deployments.
- Hosting modes: Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) and Private (VPC or on-prem) are eligible for PHI under a signed BAA.
- Hosted API (public/shared) is NOT eligible for PHI/BAA-bound workloads at this time.
- SOC 2: Redwood has a SOC 2 Type II report available under NDA; we'll share it via secure Drive link once we confirm an NDA.
- Encryption: support for customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS/HSM integrations) for Private/Dedicated deployments.
- Audit logs & retention: per-customer audit logs available; retention and export can be configured for Private and Dedicated.

Attachments I'm sharing here:
- Redwood_BAA_Draft.pdf (initial draft for your legal/security review)
- Redwood_HIPAA_FAQ.pdf (short FAQ on deployment modes and PHI boundaries)

Proposed next steps
1) Please confirm whether MedWise will proceed with Dedicated or Private mode (we can scope both; Private on VPC is common).
2) If you want, we'll start your vendor security questionnaire. I've CC'd Dev (SE) to help answer the technical questions.
3) Sign an NDA if you want the SOC 2 report shared (I'll drop the Drive link to the report after NDA).
4) Share your questionnaire (I saw you attached v2 in the meeting). We'll aim to return a completed questionnaire within 4-5 business days after we have the full doc.

Happy to hop on a 30 minute follow-up to run through any of the above. Proposed times: Thu 11/26 10-11am PT or Mon 11/30 9-10am PT.

Hi Katie  thanks for the questions. Short answers below; Dev and I can fill in any details from the questionnaire after we have it.

1) Hosted API eligibility
- Hosted (shared) endpoints are not approved for PHI even under a BAA. The isolation and controls required for PHI are provided only in Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) and Private (VPC or on-prem) deployments.

2) Logging & token retention
- By default, we do not persist full request/response bodies for Dedicated or Private customers beyond what's required for operational health.
- For Dedicated/Private, telemetry and logs can be configured to minimize sensitive fields; you control whether full payloads are stored. We can provide exportable, filtered audit logs for your security team.

3) Retention windows
- Default audit log retention: 90 days.
- Default model telemetry retention: 30 days.
- Both retention windows are configurable for Dedicated/Private customers; we can set custom retention and export policies as part of onboarding.

4) KMS/HSM / encryption
- Supported: customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS) for Dedicated and Private. HSM-backed key stores supported for Private/on-prem.
- All traffic is TLS 1.2+ in transit; data at rest is encrypted by default.

5) SOC 2 and reports
- Redwood has a SOC 2 Type II report available. We can share it under a mutual NDA / secure link.

6) Subprocessors & BAA redlines
- We are open to reviewing reasonable redlines, particularly around deletion timelines and subprocessors. We maintain a subprocessors list and will share it; final language may require legal review.

Next steps/owners
- Dev (cc'd) will be the primary technical contact to complete the questionnaire.
- Marissa will coordinate legal and BAA redline exchanges.
- We recommend a 30-45 minute follow-up with your security engineer and Dev to go through questionnaire sections A-D. Proposed: Mon 11/30 9:00am PT (Marissa suggested this)  does that work for you?

Thanks
